closure_unit.outcome: POST /kernel/product_screenshot_capture/execute only runs for an authenticated account session that holds the screenshot-capture capability; everyone else is denied before any process starts, and an authorized run is attributable to the session principal and its child process is always reclaimed.

specification_anchor_refs.verbatim: 6. Authorization is deny-by-default and evaluated on every executable backend boundary. Hiding UI rows is a projection behavior, never the security boundary.

Application authorization remains required for action semantics and capability checks; record-user table/field permissions plus ResourceBroker are the non-bypassable product data boundary, not the only policy layer.

Anonymous: a request without a valid account session token + live channel binding returns HTTP 401 (Operator 2026-09-23: 'anonymous -> 401'), and no process is spawned (no `node --version` pre-flight either). This status is route-local: do NOT change api::authority::constant_denial (403) used by every other route.

Authenticated account WITHOUT the capability `kernel.product_screenshot_capture.execute` in the session's delegated_capabilities returns HTTP 403 with the constant body {"error":"HSK-403-PROTECTED-RESOURCE"}, and no process is spawned. Deny by default: an absent, empty or unreadable capability list is a denial. Wildcards are not accepted (setup_local_owner already rejects '*' at storage/surreal/local_accounts.rs:374-375 @ab618f46).

Authorized (session holds the capability): the capture runs; the response keeps its current shape (schema_id hsk.kernel.product_screenshot_capture_execute_result@1, artifact, durable_receipt, proof, receipt) and the receipt/proof record the session principal (actor id + session id) as the initiator, not a constant or header value.

Process safety: the request body may no longer choose the executable or script. `node_binary` and `adapter_script_path` in ProductScreenshotCaptureExecuteRequest are ignored or rejected (400) when they differ from the server-side defaults ('node' resolved by the server; app/scripts/handshake-screenshot-capture.mjs); the handler never executes a caller-supplied path. The child process (kernel/product_screenshot_capture.rs:561 pre-flight and :590-606 adapter) runs off the async executor (spawn_blocking or tokio::process), has a wall-clock timeout, is killed and waited on (reaped) on timeout or request cancellation, keeps hide_console_window (no foreground window, Codex CX-SAFE-002), and a timeout returns a typed error, never a hang.

Negative tests exist and pass against the real router and real account-session store: anonymous -> 401 and zero spawns; account without capability -> 403 and zero spawns; authorized -> runs (or returns the typed AdapterDependencyMissing when node/playwright are absent - the test asserts the authorization passed, i.e. the error is not 401/403) and the result/receipt carries the session principal; caller-supplied node_binary/adapter_script_path -> not executed; a hung adapter is killed and reaped within the timeout (use a server-side test hook for the timeout value and a script that sleeps, placed under the owner TMP dir - no network, no foreground).

implementation_steps.step: Verify branch and clean worktree. Read api/kernel.rs:378-409 and kernel/product_screenshot_capture.rs:537-620 @ab618f46 (locate by fn name if lines moved).

Authentication: in execute_product_screenshot_capture_api take State<AppState> + HeaderMap and call api::authority::authenticated_session_credentials (authority.rs:1031). On Err return 401 with body {"error":"HSK-401-SESSION-REQUIRED"} (route-local; do not touch constant_denial). Do this before anything else.

Capability: read the session's delegated_capabilities (add the field to LocalSessionContext in storage/surreal/local_accounts.rs:125-131 if absent, populated from the authenticated_sessions row that authenticate_local_session already reads). If it does not contain exactly `kernel.product_screenshot_capture.execute`, return 403 constant body. Absent/empty = deny.

Remove caller control of the executable: ignore/reject request.node_binary and request.adapter_script_path unless equal to the server defaults (AC-155-5); keep the fields in the type only if removing them breaks deserialisation of existing callers (then reject non-default values with 400).

Process lifecycle: run both Command invocations with a bounded wall-clock timeout (constant in product_screenshot_capture.rs, e.g. 120 s, with a test-only override), kill + wait on expiry, keep hide_console_window, and move the blocking work to tokio::task::spawn_blocking (or tokio::process with kill_on_drop(true)). Map a timeout to a typed ProductScreenshotExecutionError variant (no new StorageError variants involved).

Attribution: pass the session actor id and session id into the receipt/proof construction (capture_product_screenshot_from_browser_adapter's command_or_api_ref / receipt fields) so the returned receipt names the initiator.

Tests: create tests/mt155_product_screenshot_capture_route_auth_tests.rs using account_session_support + an AppState built like tests/atelier_stealth_window_tests.rs:265 (without the Option skip), serving api::kernel routes on 127.0.0.1:0. Tests: mt155_anonymous_capture_is_401_and_spawns_nothing, mt155_account_without_capability_is_403_and_spawns_nothing, mt155_authorized_capture_passes_authorization_and_is_attributed, mt155_caller_supplied_binary_is_never_executed, mt155_hung_adapter_is_killed_and_reaped_within_timeout. 'Spawns nothing' is proven by a sentinel: point the (rejected) caller path at a script that would create a marker file under the owner TMP dir and assert the marker never appears; for the default path assert no adapter-output file is created.

risks: Arbitrary code execution: the body chooses node_binary and adapter_script_path today.
Blocking Command::output() on the async executor starves other requests; no timeout means orphaned/hung node processes.
Checking the capability after the pre-flight `node --version` still spawns a process for denied callers.
Changing constant_denial to 401 globally would change every other route's contract and C2's proofs.

The artifact root is resolved relative to the process working directory ("../Handshake_Artifacts/...") - Codex CX-984-001 forbids cwd-relative resolution; recorded as residual unless the fix is trivially within this route (use the configured HANDSHAKE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT).
minimum_controls: Every positive proof runs as an authenticated record user (account session + channel binding). A root/admin session (with_admin_operation, test_admin_query*, SurrealStorage without with_record_user_scope) may only SEED preconditions that the product itself cannot create, and never counts as privacy/isolation proof (02:2773, LM-RLS-002).

Every changed route has: anonymous negative (no session headers), cross-account negative (a second OwnerSession cannot read or write the first account's rows, and the rows are unchanged afterwards), and where a write is involved, a read-only (viewer) negative when the grant model can express one.
Denied writes are proven by re-reading the canonical row after the call (F3: denied writes are silent). A 403 status alone is not proof that nothing was written.

Anti-scaffold: no new abstraction, trait, feature flag, config knob or helper that is not called by product code in this MT; no `#[ignore]`, no `return Ok(())` skip paths, no assertion weakened or deleted to go green; tests may not assert only on mocks/fixtures the Coder authored for a resource-boundary claim (CODER-PROOF-004, CODER-CODE-006).

No fixture-only proof: each acceptance item is proven against the real embedded SurrealDB store (fresh Handshake-managed RocksDB/SurrealKV directory under the owner runtime root), through the real axum router, with the real ResourceBroker.

Every test binary run must report a NONZERO executed count for the named tests (`running N tests` with N equal to the number of names passed with --exact); a `0 passed` result is a failure of the check, not a pass.
Spawn-count proof: denied tests assert zero processes via a marker file, not by status code alone.

The reclaim test proves the child PID is gone after the timeout (e.g. the marker script writes its PID; assert the process no longer exists via sysinfo/tasklist in-test) - never kill a process the test did not start.
